title: Savitch's theorem: lots of work, very little memory
sub: Deciding reachability by trying midpoints. The call stack is reused over and over, so memory stays tiny while the work balloons.

frames.caption: A configuration graph: can c0 reach c4 within 4 steps? Savitch's idea: guess a midpoint and split the path in half, recursively.

frames.caption: Answer: yes. It took 35 calls, but the stack never held more than 3 frames. Each frame stores two configurations, and halving makes it only log(t) deep: that's why NSPACE(s) ⊆ DSPACE(s²).
